newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ consumers' outlook relatively stable - Westpac.
newsitem.headline: NZ consumers' outlook relatively stable - Westpac.

text.p: Consumers' long-term outlook for the New Zealand economy has remained relatively stable, Wesptac said in a commentary on the Westpac McDermott September quarter consumer confidence survey published on Friday.
A net 34.8 percent of respondents to the survey have a positive outlook for the economy over the next five years, an improvement of 2.9 percent points from June but down 3.2 percent from a year ago.
The net number of respondents reporting that it was a good time to buy a major household item increased by 3.7 points over June but was still nine points lower than a year ago.
The residential building market continues to report signs of reduced activity growth in line with the general trend downward in consumer confidence, Westpac said.
"Whilst we do not expect to see substantial falls in indicators of property market demand and price, we similarly feel that the market has reached a plateau," it said.
"However, confidence levels indicate that it is possible we may see some resurgence in property market activity once uncertainty surrounding the election outcome is out the way."
Consumers' estimates of the current level of inflation showed little change in the quarter.
In September, the average estimate for current inflation was 3.3 percent compared with 3.5 percent a year ago.

Expectations with regard to the future direction of inflation have shifted towards a lower outlook over the quarter, but higher than a year ago. The net number of respondents expecting inflation to increase fell to eight points from June, still 13 points higher than in September in September.
However, the actual expected level of inflation for the next year has improved both on a quarterly and annual basis.
The average expected inflation rate over the next year measured 4.3 percent against 4.5 percent a year ago.

Intended use of a $5,000 windfall remained relatively constant over the year with a small increase in intentions to pay off mortgages and other debts, purchases of shares and growth in spending intentions.
Respondents showed little change in their use of different forms of savings over the last quarter except for the real estate category which fell by seven points.

Over the year, all categories of savings fell with the exception of the "no savings" category which recorded a small increase. Westpac said it expects the labour market to have peaked around current levels.
